publisher: State legislatures and code publishers (each row names its statute and page)
vintage: Codes as published online, read October 23, 2026
table: Local recall timing bars by state: days into a term before a petition may be filed, days before the term's end after which none may be, and the bar after a failed recall
title: When a local recall petition may be filed, by state
universe: Elected local officers (city and county) in places whose municipal rule pack gives a petitioned recall
geography: All 56 places, keyed by postal code
limits: Statute text only, no case law. Places whose rule pack gives no petitioned local recall carry no bar. "encoded" is the row written to src/core2/data/campaigns/recall-bars.json (days; six calendar months stored as 182 days and two as 61, ESTIMATED with the 181 to 184 and 59 to 62 days those months span, SG-GOV-recall-bars-calendar-months); scripts/research/check-core-research.ts fails when the two differ. "afterFailed" is what each statute says about a later petition; the recall engine still applies one rule everywhere (none again in the term after one failed) until the builder item gov-recall-bars-election-clock reads it.

quotes: No petition to recall any member of the governing body of a municipality shall be filed until the member has served one-fourth of his or her term of office.
FL.estimatedFrom: The statute bars a petition until one-fourth of the term is served: term years x 365 / 4 days, which is 182.5 days of a two-year term, 273.75 of a three-year term and 365 of a four-year term. The engine's day count is two values, 183 days for a term of two years or less and 365 for a longer one (longTermOpeningDays), so it equals the statute for a two-year term (within half a day) and a four-year term, is 91 days long (365 against 273.75) for a three-year term, and would be 183 days short (365 against 547.5) for a six-year term. The spread, 182 to 365 days, is the statute's bar for terms of 2, 3 and 4 years, the lengths the game reads for local seats: the 18 seat terms in src/core2/gov-rules/municipal-governments.json are all 2, 3 or 4 years, and the modal council term (ICMA 2018, 63.6% of at-large councils), the default mayor term and the state's county schedule (data/research/government/county-election-schedule-by-state.json) are each 4 years. No compiled charter reading for this state carries a term length, so today its council, mayor and county commission seats take four years, where the engine is exact; the 91-day gap appears for a three-year term (13.1% of at-large councils in the ICMA 2018 table). Registered as SG-GOV-recall-bars-term-fraction; the builder item gov-recall-bars-fraction-of-term encodes a fraction-of-term bar.
FL.afterFailed: not stated in the sections read

quotes: no recall petition may be submitted for certification to or accepted for certification by the registrar of voters or any other official if less than six months remain in the term of office.
LA.encodingNote: No bar at the start of the term in the section read; six months taken as 182 days.
LA.afterFailed: not stated in the sections read
LA.estimatedFrom: The statute counts six calendar months before the term ends; the bar table holds days (closingDays), so the row stores 182. Six calendar months span 181 to 184 days depending on the date counted from (month lengths and leap years, computed over a four-year cycle), so a bar of 182 days is up to 1 day longer or 2 days shorter than the statute's on a given date: for a term ending January 1, six months before is July 1, 184 days earlier, so 182 days admits two days the statute bars. Registered as SG-GOV-recall-bars-calendar-months; the builder item gov-recall-bars-calendar-months reads bars in calendar months.

MT.afterFailed: two years after a recall election, unless its cost is reimbursed
MT.estimatedFrom: The statute counts two calendar months after the term begins; the bar table holds days (openingDays), so the row stores 61. Two calendar months span 59 to 62 days depending on the date counted from (month lengths and leap years, computed over a four-year cycle), so a bar of 61 days is up to 2 days longer or 1 day shorter than the statute's on a given date: for a term beginning January 1 of a common year the statute's bar ends on March 1, 59 days in. Registered as SG-GOV-recall-bars-calendar-months; the builder item gov-recall-bars-calendar-months reads bars in calendar months.

quotes: the filing officer shall call a special election to be held not sooner than ninety-five days nor later than one hundred five days following the date the filing officer certifies the petition valid and sufficient.

A member is not subject to recall twice during the term for which the member was elected. A member whose office is on the ballot at a regularly scheduled election occurring within one year is not subject to recall if the recall special election would occur within one year of the next regularly scheduled election in which the member could be re-elected.
ND.estimatedFrom: No bar at the start of the term. The end bar falls on the recall election, held 95 to 105 days after the petition is certified, which must be more than a year before the next regular election: a petition filed fewer than about 365 + 100 = 465 days before that election cannot be voted on. The bar table counts days before the term's end, which comes some weeks after that election, so 465 is the low end and 500 allows for the gap.
ND.afterFailed: not twice in the same term
